### Describe the bug
As said in that [issue](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/7644), TestServer have to consider with option `AllowSynchronousIO`. But it doesn't work.

### To Reproduce
To reproduce you are able to run the test in the attached project [AllowSynchronousIOInTestServerReproduce.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/files/5760952/AllowSynchronousIOInTestServerReproduce.zip) or just to insert that code in a project which has references to NuGet packages (xUnit 2.4.1 and Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost 3.1.10)
```
[Fact]
public async Task ExampleTest()
{
    using var host = await new HostBuilder().ConfigureWebHost(webBuilder =>
    {
        webBuilder
            .UseTestServer()
            .ConfigureServices(services =>
            {
                services.Configure<TestServer>(options => options.AllowSynchronousIO = true);
            })
            .Configure(app =>
            {
                app.Use(async (context, next) =>
                {
                    context.Request.Body.ReadByte();

                    await next.Invoke();
                });
            });
    }).StartAsync();
    var httpClient = host.GetTestClient();

    var response = await httpClient.GetAsync("/");

    Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.NotFound, response.StatusCode);
}
```

@Tratcher Thanks, your code works. So the reason for this issue is a misunderstanding of how `services.Configure<TestServer>` works.
Please, could you explain why `IISServerOptions`, `KesterOptions`, and `HttpSysOptions` exist, but `TestServerOptions` not?

We've moved this issue to the Backlog milestone. This means that it is not going to be worked on for the coming release. We will reassess the backlog following the current release and consider this item at that time. To learn more about our issue management process and to have better expectation regarding different types of issues you can read our [Triage Process](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/docs/TriageProcess.md).
Triage note: TestServerOptions sounds like a good idea. That's why we've added the "help wanted" label.

> Please, could you explain why `IISServerOptions`, `KesterOptions`, and `HttpSysOptions` exist, but `TestServerOptions` not?

History mostly. TestServer predates all of those other servers and the options pattern. The TestServer used to be created using a different pattern.
https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetKatana/blob/1fba52940ccfa74470c75c627699baca13aadfa4/src/Microsoft.Owin.Testing/TestServer.cs#L63

If we add the options type we should also add the overload `.UseTestServer(options => {})`
